      "duration": 0.1

      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- Most bash commands should end with a newline (\n) to cause them to execute
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Your task is to create a file /app/src/program.cbl in which there will be a new COBOL program in fixed format, 
which will be run from the /app/src directory and should be compiled and executed using GnuCOBOL 3.  
Do not include ">>SOURCE FORMAT IS FIXED". Keep each line ≤ 80 characters. The compiler will use fixed format by default.
The program will run from /app/src directory and must compile with GnuCOBOL 3. File /app/src/INPUT.DAT already exist.
  Processes mortgage applications. Checks terms and generates a payment schedule. The program reads the existing file at /app/src/INPUT.DAT.
  ID - X(10) NAME - X(30) LOAN-AMOUNT - 9(10) PROPERTY-VALUE - 9(10) DOWN-PAYMENT - 9(10) TERM - 9(2) RATE - 9(3)V9(2) separated by the symbol ';'.
  Calculates the minimum down payment (15% of the property value). If the client's down payment is less, the application is rejected.
  For approved applications, the monthly payment is calculated using the annuity nominal formula and a full payment schedule is generated.
  The results are written to the file at /app/data/OUTPUT.DAT: ID - X(10) STATUS - X(5) (REASON - X(50) in case of refusal)
    For rejected applications: ID and reason for rejection.
    For approved applications: ID and  «APPRO\n» and detailed payment schedule:
    MON-NUMBER - 9(3) PAYMENT-AMOUNT, INTEREST-PART, PRINCIPAL-PART - 9(8).99 REMAINING-BALANCE - 9(10).99.(without header).
    - CALCULATIONS: 
        MIN_DOWN = PROP_VALUE * 0.15
        MONTHLY_RATE = INTEREST_RATE / 1200
        MONTHLY_PAYMENT = LOAN_AMOUNT * monthly_rate / (1 - (1 + monthly_rate)**(-term_months))
        Use ROUNDED for all financial computations.
  Success Criteria:
    A correctly constructed payment schedule in the file output. Example output file:
     «TEST000001DENY INSUFFICIENT FUNDS FOR DOWN PAYMENT
      TEST000002APPRO
      001 00000400.00 00000022.92 00000377.08 0000004622.92 etc.»

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN-LOGIC.
    OPEN INPUT IN-FILE
    OPEN OUTPUT OUT-FILE
    PERFORM UNTIL EOF-FLAG = 'Y'
        READ IN-FILE
            AT END MOVE 'Y' TO EOF-FLAG
        NOT AT END
            PERFORM PROCESS-RECORD
        END-READ
    END-PERFORM
    CLOSE IN-FILE
    CLOSE OUT-FILE
    STOP RUN.
PROCESS-RECORD.
    UNSTRING IN-REC DELIMITED BY ';'

             WS-NAME
             WS-LOAN-AMOUNT
             WS-PROP-VALUE
             WS-DOWN-PAYMENT
             WS-TERM
             WS-RATE
    END-UNSTRING
    COMPUTE WS-MIN-DOWN = WS-PROP-VALUE * 0.15 ROUNDED
    IF WS-DOWN-PAYMENT < WS-MIN-DOWN

        STRING WS-ID DELIMITED BY SIZE
               WS-SPACE
               WS-REASON DELIMITED BY SIZE
               INTO OUT-REC
        END-STRING
        WRITE OUT-REC
    ELSE
        MOVE WS-LOAN-AMOUNT TO WS-BALANCE
        COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-RATE = WS-RATE / 1200
        COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-PAYMENT = WS-LOAN-AMOUNT *
            WS-MONTHLY-RATE /

        STRING WS-ID DELIMITED BY SIZE
               'APPRO' DELIMITED BY SIZE
               INTO OUT-REC
        END-STRING
        WRITE OUT-REC
        PERFORM VARYING WS-MONTH-NUM FROM 1 BY 1
                UNTIL WS-MONTH-NUM > WS-TERM
            COMPUTE WS-INTEREST-PART =
                WS-BALANCE * WS-MONTHLY-RATE ROUNDED
            COMPUTE WS-PRINCIPAL-PART =
                WS-MONTHLY-PAYMENT - WS-INTEREST-PART ROUNDED
            COMPUTE WS-BALANCE = WS-BALANCE -
                WS-PRINCIPAL-PART ROUNDED
            MOVE WS-MONTHLY-PAYMENT TO WS-MONTHLY-PAY-ED
            MOVE WS-INTEREST-PART TO WS-INTEREST-ED
            MOVE WS-PRINCIPAL-PART TO WS-PRINCIPAL-ED
            MOVE WS-BALANCE TO WS-BALANCE-ED
            STRING WS-MONTH-NUM DELIMITED BY SIZE
                   WS-SPACE
                   WS-MONTHLY-PAY-ED DELIMITED BY SIZE
                   WS-SPACE
                   WS-INTEREST-ED DELIMITED BY SIZE
                   WS-SPACE
                   WS-PRINCIPAL-ED DELIMITED BY SIZE
                   WS-SPACE
                   WS-BALANCE-ED DELIMITED BY SIZE
                   INTO OUT-REC
            END-STRING
            WRITE OUT-REC
        END-PERFORM
    END-IF.
EOF
